transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-03 10:00 UTC / Duration ~45m / Attendees: Alex, Samira (Redwood), Diego, Maya (Redwood), Priya, Ben, Carmen, Jordan (NovaPay)

Summary (auto): throughput optimization check-in, config changes tested last week (continuous batching enabled), observed CPU/GPU utilization, discussed queueing and tail latency.

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — run through last week's benchmark results, tuning notes on continuous batching and queue/conc settings, and agree next steps.
[00:20] Priya Nair: thanks Alex, yep; we ran your patch on staging yesterday. saw higher throughput but a few 500s when we pushed to about, uh, 1.2k rps.
[00:32] Samira Patel: right, so the continuous-batcher reduced per-token overhead, so token/sec improved about 28% at the mid-range. but from the logs it looks like at peaks the internal request queue starts to starve the workers, we get retries, and the autoscaler doesn't react quick enough.
[00:48] Ben Thompson: yeah we saw queue lengths spike, and some timeouts at ~1100 qps, which is below our target 2k peak. wonder if the concurrency knob is still too low.
[01:05] Maya Li: just to add, we also toggled the quantization profile to q4f16 on the staging model — slight latency bump on cold calls but batch throughput was higher. might be a tradeoff for tail latency.
[01:22] Priya Nair: by cold calls you mean first token response, right? that's important for our chat product.
[01:28] Samira Patel: yes exactly, cold-start latency a bit higher but once cache warmed we see much better tokens/sec. would recommend experiment with KV cache TTLs and prefix caching for common prompts.
[01:40] Carmen Ortiz: can you remind us the difference between continuous batching and the older fixed-window batching? we tested both last month and results were mixed.
[01:49] Alex Chen: sure — fixed-window batches requests in a fixed window e.g., 20ms which helps with predictable latency but wastes opportunity when QPS varies. continuous batching tries to keep the GPU busy by merging requests up to a size limit while respecting per-request latency SLOs; better overall throughput but can increase tail latency if queues build up.
[02:12] Jordan Lee: are we hitting a CPU bottleneck or GPU? our metrics showed high CPU on the request router when we scaled concurrency.
[02:20] Samira Patel: good call — in the 5/27 run the router CPU peaked; we think serialization and grpc overhead at high concurrency was the limiter. we suggested moving some pre-processing to a separate pool and enabling gRPC batch compression to reduce CPU.
[02:36] Ben Thompson: ok that aligns; we can offload a bit on our side. Priya, any insight from the traces you ran?
[02:42] Priya Nair: traces show sequence length distribution skewed toward 120 tokens median, but about 10% are 800-1200 tokens which is hurting tail. we can share anonymized traces.
[02:55] Alex Chen: perfect — that will help Samira pick batch size targets and queue timeouts.
[03:08] Samira Patel: on the cluster side, recommended conc targets to try: 8, 16, 32 per worker for your model family. also suggested queue-limit of 200 requests with backpressure on overflow, and a per-request timeout of 12s to avoid long tail stalls.
[03:26] Priya Nair: 12s sounds ok, though for interactive chat we'd prefer lower. is there a config that can favour short requests?
[03:33] Maya Li: yes — priority queues: you can tag requests with priority based on endpoint/route. short chat messages can be routed to a fast lane with stricter batch size limit and lower wait threshold. longer generation routes go to throughput lane.
[03:48] Carmen Ortiz: do we need Dedicated for this or can Hosted handle it with tuning? cost is a factor for us.
[03:55] Alex Chen: hosted with these optimizations can hit your mid-range SLOs, but your peak 2k QPS with long tails and compliance needs might push you to Dedicated for isolation and predictable capacity. we can show a cost/latency comparison after the benchmark runs.
[04:08] Priya Nair: ok good. what about KV cache? you mentioned prefix caching — how big a win is that?
[04:14] Samira Patel: in our internal tests, prefix/KV cache cut average tokens-caused compute by about 20% for repeated prompts. For you, if ~40% of requests are similar prompts we could see notable cost reduction and reduced latency.
[04:29] Ben Thompson: do we need extra infra for the cache? like Redis or can you handle it internally?
[04:34] Samira Patel: Redwood's runtime supports in-process KV cache and an optional external Redis for larger state; for Private deployments we'd integrate with your Redis in the VPC. For hosted we can use managed cache — details in the security doc.
[04:50] Priya Nair: security is key; Carmen will want SOC2 matrix.
[04:54] Carmen Ortiz: yes send SOC2 and SSO/SAML docs.
[04:57] Alex Chen: will do — action item.
[05:02] Diego Ruiz: quick note on the benchmark results we shared: csv link in the deck, but tl;dr — baseline (no continuous-batcher) at 16 conc: 650 requests/sec, after batching: ~830 rps, and with q4f16 + kv warm ~980 rps. tail p95 increased from 180ms to 240ms at midrange but p99 stays high when the queue spikes.
[05:28] Ben Thompson: the p99s are the worry; our SLAs target <500ms p99.
[05:32] Samira Patel: agree; we think queue trimming + priority lanes + smaller batches for short requests will reduce p99. Also need to tune autoscaler thresholds so additional workers spawn before queue passes critical length.
[05:50] Priya Nair: what's the recommended autoscaler policy? we're on GKE for this POC.
[05:56] Maya Li: recommended policy: scale-up at queue-length > 120 for 30s sustained, add 1-2 pods per event, and a cooldown of 2m. Pre-warming a small dedicated pool for peak windows also helps.
[06:10] Jordan Lee: are warm instances persisted across scale events? the cold start is painful.
[06:15] Samira Patel: warm instances hold model weights in GPU memory; scaling adds new pods which need to load weights — that's where pre-warm helps. we can also keep a minimum pod count to reduce cold starts.
[06:28] Priya Nair: for the next benchmark can you test min-pods 2 vs 4 and report cold-start failures?
[06:33] Alex Chen: yup, included in the plan. Samira will run: conc 8/16/32 x min-pods 2/4 x queue-limits 100/200 and push CSVs.
[06:45] Carmen Ortiz: one more on compliance — do you provide audit logs per request? some of our legal team needs request-level auditability.
[06:51] Diego Ruiz: yes we capture request metadata and can integrate with your SIEM; for Private we keep full logs on customer infra, for Hosted we stream to a secure retention bucket. we'll share the log retention options.
[07:06] Priya Nair: thanks. can you add cost per qps estimate after the scaling runs? that's key for our procurement team.
[07:12] Alex Chen: sure — we'll produce cost per 1k qps baseline and optimized.
[07:19] Ben Thompson: last question: any vendor lock if we choose Dedicated? we want portability.
[07:24] Maya Li: Dedicated is infrastructure we manage for you; model artifacts and configs are standard, and we support export of config + model pins so you can move. but managed tooling ties some operational glue. We'll include portability notes.
[07:38] Priya Nair: ok sounds good.
[07:42] Alex Chen: recap / next steps — run 1-hour benchmarks at multiple concurrencies & min-pods, share CSV and tuned configs, NovaPay to provide traces and confirm VPC egress, Redwood to send SOC2/SSO docs and cost estimates. Follow-up demo Tue 2026-06-09 10am UTC (tentative).
[08:02] Carmen Ortiz: confirmed tentative on our calendar.
[08:10] Alex Chen: awesome thanks team. we'll send notes and artifacts after call.
